text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Bosnian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Alija Izetbegovic, chairman of the Bosnian presidency, said during his visit to Moslem holy site of Ajvatovica that Bosnia deserves international aid for reconstruction because the world prevented the government from defending itself during the war. - Izetbegovic asked Croatian President Franjo Tudjman to postpone meeting between the two leaders, scheduled for June 30 in Split. Izetbegovic's office accused Croatian side of failing to implement agreed measures, including the formation of a joint Moslem-Croat police force in the Mostar area, and of failing to address several unresolved issues.
- Croatia insisted on the meeting for the sake of publicity and not with the intention of solving any vital issue, says statement from Izetbegovic's office.
- Croatian President Franjo Tudjman's office says the Izetbegovic-Tudjman meeting was postponed due to request by Izetbegovic. The Croatian side will propose the meeting to be held in about ten days.

- Co-chairman of the Council of Ministers Haris Silajdzic told U.S. congressman Paul McHale that he believes Washington will remain engaged in the implementation of the Dayton peace accord even after American troops withdraw from the country.

- Ivan Mijacevic, a parliament member of the opposition Social Democratic Party and former commander of a Bosnian army brigade, was released from a prison in the Serb-controlled town of Doboj after being held for seven weeks, local radio reported. Mijacevic, a Croat, was arrested as he was driving through Bosnian Serb territory and authorities had threatened to try him for alleged war crimes.

- The Iranian ambassador to Croatia was attacked near Brcko on Saturday by three unidentified people, according to sources in the Iranian Embassy in Sarajevo. Due to injuries to his head and face, the ambassador was taken to Brcko hospital and his embassy car was stolen. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
